source_bindings.label: def:test-categories
source_bindings.literal_latex: \begin{definition}[The test categories] \label{def:test-categories} Let $\Tzero(X)$ be the smallest full replete triangulated subcategory of $\mathsf D(X)$ containing \begin{equation} \label{cat:generators} Rf_*\const{\R}{B}, \qquad f:B\longrightarrow X, \qquad B\text{ a compact finite polyhedron}, \end{equation} where $f$ is any continuous map. Let $\T(X)$ be its closure under direct summands in $\mathsf D(X)$. When $X$ has a specified semialgebraic model, define $\Pzero(X)$ and $\Pcat(X)$ in the same manner, requiring $B$ to be a compact polyhedron in a Euclidean space and $f$ to be continuous semialgebraic in the specified models. For an arbitrary open subset $U$ of a semialgebraic model, the condition on $f:B\to U$ is that its composite into that model be semialgebraic. The open subset itself need not be semialgebraic. An allowed map for $\T$ is a continuous map of test spaces. For $\Pcat$ we use continuous semialgebraic maps in the models, their restrictions to the open subsets under consideration, and inclusions of such open subsets. The condition on a map used in the arguments below is that composition carry every allowed compact-source generator to an allowed compact-source generator. Homotopies for $\Pcat$ satisfy this condition in their two variables; the continuous semialgebraic homotopies used below do so. \end{definition}

source_bindings.label: lem:cutoff
source_bindings.literal_latex: \begin{lemma}[Cutoff] \label{lem:cutoff} Let $K\subset O\subset X$, where $K$ is closed in $X$ and $O$ is open. For every $A\in\Bzero(X)$ there is a morphism \[ s:A'\longrightarrow A \] such that $A'$ is extended from $\Bzero(O)$, its cohomology vanishes outside a compact subset of $O$, and $s$ restricts to an isomorphism on some open neighborhood of $K$. \end{lemma}

source_bindings.label: thm:germs
source_bindings.literal_latex: \begin{theorem}[Germ description] \label{thm:germs} Restriction induces natural isomorphisms \[ \Hom_{\Bcat(X)/\Bcat(U)}(A,B) \simeq \operatorname*{colim}_{N\supset X\setminus U} \Hom_{\mathsf D(N)}(A|_N,B|_N) \] for every $A,B\in\Bcat(X)$. These isomorphisms respect composition, open restriction of duality, and restriction of distinguished triangles. The quotient here is the Verdier quotient itself. \end{theorem}

source_bindings.label: prop:open-cover
source_bindings.literal_latex: \begin{proposition}[An open cover gives a dense inclusion] \label{prop:open-cover} If $X=U\cup V$ with $U,V$ open, extension by zero induces a fully faithful exact functor preserving duality \begin{equation} \label{loc:eq-open-cover} \Bcat(V)/\Bcat(U\cap V) \longrightarrow\Bcat(X)/\Bcat(U). \end{equation} Its replete image is dense: every object of the target is an actual summand of an object in the image. These functors commute with $\Pcat\to\T$. \end{proposition}

source_bindings.label: thm:bounded-comparison
source_bindings.literal_latex: \begin{theorem}[Bounded comparison] \label{thm:bounded-comparison} For every $j\ge0$ there is a nonnegative integer $e_j$, independent of $r$, such that the kernel and cokernel of \[ F_r(S^j)\longrightarrow E_r(S^j) \] are annihilated by $2^{e_j}$ for every integer $r$. \end{theorem}
